opening.argument: The strongest evidence is the presentation itself: the video tracks programming-language popularity from 1965 to 2019 through changing bar-chart rankings. The description defines popularity by the share of programmers proficient in or learning a language, and explains that the ranking draws on indexes, repository access data, surveys, and publication frequency. That is an educational account of how the timeline was assembled. The request to support the channel is ordinary audience support; nothing in the cited material links it to an investment offer, required payment, credential collection, or promised return. A careful reading should treat the request in the context of the ranking actually shown, without inferring a financial scheme from it.

citations.quote: For recent years I've used multiple programming languages popularity indexes with adjustments thanks to the data from GitHub repositories access frequency.
Please support my channel. It can buy me another cup of coffee :)
